and there is no “oracle of the Lord” or “word of the Lord” there. / It is one Lord who interpreted His word through the mouth of His true ones, / some by symbol and some by plain and open speech. / In straightforward speech Ahijah heard his Lord’s command, / and tore the garment that covered him into twelve pieces. / In an open revelation of the Spirit this Shilonite received it, / and gave the son of Nebat ten pieces of his garment. / Here the deed was done openly, and not in mystery, / for Jeroboam openly took ten pieces. / Openly Elijah too held back heaven and earth, / and by his deeds he restrained the air from its course. / Openly he received food, openly, from the mouths of ravens, / and with his limbs he walked and came to the widow of Zarephath. / Openly he multiplied flour and oil in the widow’s house, / and he lived, and gave life, as He willed who willed it. / Openly he snatched a dead man, openly, from the mouth of death, / and before everyone’s eyes he set the sacrifices ablaze and brought down fire. / Bodily he heard a voice and saw a vision. / With the eyes of the body he saw earthquake and fire and wind, / and after them he heard the voice of gentle speech. / These things the Tishbite received openly, / and he turned to go down toward the goal that had been shown him. / Here let no one fashion insipid riddles, / but let him receive these things openly, as they were spoken. / This is open and pure speech, without deceit, / and there is in it no likeness of dream visions understood spiritually. / By this way of open words Elisha went, / and received the Spirit and worked mighty deeds before the eyes of onlookers. / Before the eyes of onlookers he healed the waters with salt and a bowl, / and sent wood after the iron and drew it up to the surface.

With an open word he cursed the boys who mocked him for nothing, / and bears came out and tore them without pity. / Without deceit he gave a child to the Shunammite, / and when the child suddenly died, he returned and raised him from the house of the dead. / By this same order he multiplied water in a desert place, / and gave provision to the three kings who were in need. / And in the same way he sweetened the bitterness that was in the pot, / and multiplied bread and made a plenty beyond the ordinary. / With the eye of the body he saw the spiritual beings surrounding him, / and struck the Edomites with bewilderment and blinded them. / In an open revelation of the Spirit he saw the messenger who came to put him to death, / and foretold that the siege would cease and there would be plenty. / In one bodily act he made the king hold a bow in his hand, / and showed him that he would defeat the Edomites three times. / The bodiless Spirit gave breath through him after his death, / and raised the dead man who by chance touched his remains. / That command which gave him the double portion of prophecy / itself worked by his hands kinds of signs higher than he. / Very lofty are the kinds of revelations the righteous received, / and how much lowlier is human weakness than such things! / This glory Isaiah saw within the temple, / and he grieved and lamented over the wretchedness of human nature. / “Woe is me, the wretched!” the righteous one said before the revelation, / “for my lips are unclean, and unclean are the people of my fathers’ house.” / Spiritually he saw the vision that was shown to him, / and was amazed and astonished at the greatness of the sight and the lowliness of man. / A fearful sight full of wonder Isaiah saw: / the King who is over all, and the hosts that glorify Him. / Not with his eyes did he see the throne of the Godhead, / nor did he receive with his hearing the “Holy” of the seraphim. / For it was a non-bodily vision that he saw with his mind, / and the name of God was depicted within it, and not God. / God does not sit in human fashion in the temple, / nor do spiritual beings have wings like a bird. / Nor was the coal that was brought to him a coal,

but the figure of the mystery of our redemption that comes at the end. / In the mystery of redemption the seraph brought it near to his lips, / and trod the way for that mercy toward all the nations. / With tongs the bodiless one held the bodily coal, / and this is the marvel, that he stooped toward something lesser than himself. / A coal is immeasurably lesser than an angel, / so why was it that the angel stirred from his silence? / It was not the senseless coal that the Watcher honored, / but the mystery that was being announced through his stillness. / Here let us learn how great is the power of the mystery of our redemption, / that the seraph of the Spirit did not draw near to scrutinize it. / Here let the foolish brazenness of Judaism be put to shame, / who read the books and do not grasp the meaning of the books. / In shame let the bands of heretics also stand, / who do not grant that our Lord’s body was a body. / Let the righteous one who knows condemn the Kromtanites [?], / who hide the working of the body’s sufferings in the Godhead. / Let everyone stand in guilt without acquittal / who hinders me from the course along the path of my words. / Along the path of the divine visions I am eager to go, / and I hope to quicken my mind by examining them. / From the son of Amoz to the son of Beeri my word is drawn, / and I marveled greatly at the spirit of revelation that was with him. / “Go, take for yourself two despised wives, / and in their wantonness depict the evils of the two tribes.” / Without shame he accepted living with wanton women, / and showed the people how loathsome their deeds were. / “In despised women depict the likenesses of their despicableness, / and in their children [?] decree a threat over their sins. / Let the names of your children be letters against the corrupt, / so that when they are chastised they may cease a little from evils.” / Through your wives and your children he will chastise those full of iniquity,

and make known to them that there is justice and there is forgiveness. / This is the aim of the prophecy of pure Hosea, / and the inquiry into Joel’s word also resembles his. / A fearful report he made the children of his people hear, / and astonished them with the kinds of chastisements in the words of his mouth: / “Hear, you elders, and tremble, all you inhabitants of the earth, / for the time is near when you will be destroyed before the afflictions.” / Locust and crawler and cricket he called the captors, / and set them in order as chastisements, one after another. / It was not locusts that the seer of hidden things saw, / but the devastation of the Assyrians and the Babylonians. / The Assyrians he named locust and the crawler that creeps, / and the Babylonians he called the cricket that strikes and withers. / This is the force of the word of Joel, herald of the Spirit, / and mingled with his threats is the nature of the day of recompense. / Toward his aim Amos too turned, the shepherd of flocks, / and lifted his voice and chastised the People and the nations alike. / In one threat the seer bound together the People and the nations, / and taught them that His word is fulfilled through deeds. / Obadiah too confirmed his words with the voice of threat, / and humbled the might of the Edomites by the decree of his judgment. / Jonah served two things at once in his prophecy: / the overthrow of Nineveh and the repentance of all the nations. / The son of Amittai saw the turning of the nations in the punishments of Nineveh,

and he trembled and was dismayed that the nations would enter and the People go out. / The son of the Hebrews made himself a hasty fugitive, / so that he would not be called a prophet who proclaimed estrangement. / The Lord of the air sent a wind upon the fugitive, / caught him with a net [?], and brought him into his prison, the belly of the fish. / Within the confines [?] of flesh his Lord bound the hasty servant, / so that he would not learn to hate the peace of humankind. / The divine revelation called him to human peace, / and because he would not go, it buried him in the fish and raised him in a mystery. / For that descent into the sea was a mystery / of that redemption which comes at the end for all the nations. / In the mystery of the redemption of our Lord’s death the son of Amittai died, / and in the turning of the Assyrians was the life of every man. / He turned the whole of nature through the Ninevites, / and trod the way for the preaching among the nations. / So the order of his word differs from that of the prophets, / in that he did not share his prophecy with the children of his people. / Micah’s course was in the way of his fellows, / and he too interpreted the message that Amos interpreted. / He too made the children of his people hear fearful sounds, / and threatened them with the report of captivity and of return. / Spiritual was the kind of revelation of this temple of the Spirit, / and in the Spirit he announced that the Messiah comes and redeems the nations. / Nahum announced the fall of the Assyrians, / and how, when they are humbled, the People will rest from servitude. / Zeal against the wicked set righteous Habakkuk ablaze, / and he believed and affirmed that vengeance would come for his zeal.

Zephaniah sharpened the punishments of his fellows in the captivity of his people, / and turned and announced that the yoke of the kingdom of Babylon would cease. / Haggai pressed urgently for the building of the holy temple, / and told the people of the coming of the Scythians. / Lofty are the kinds of revelations in Zechariah’s prophecy, / and glorious the beauty of the fearful visions he saw in his mind. / In his mind the Spirit that chose him showed him spiritual things, / and in his thought depicted likenesses without composition. / Spiritually he saw chariots and their riders, / which were sent to destroy the nations that had humbled the People. / By the Spirit he also contemplated the lampstand of the Spirit of grace, / and not with the senses did he look upon the lamps above it. / He announced the priesthood of the People in the kinds of his visions, / that the leadership of kings and priests would be restored to them. / With two olive trees he represented priesthood and kingship, / and saw that they stood on the right and on the left. / By the names of deeds he named their names: / the one “Pleasant” and the other “Cord of [?]”. / With a sickle he depicted the decree of judgment upon all the nations, / and with horns the ways in which dominion is brought to an end. / Spiritually the prophet of the Spirit depicted everything, / and he too foretold the war of the sons of Javan. / This is the aim of the spirit of the revelations of prophecy, / and to this aim Malachi, the sealer of mysteries, turned. / Like a seal were the words of the messenger of the Spirit, / and he sealed the words of prophecy and of apostleship.

The Spirit showed him the coming of the Antichrist, / and how the Tishbite comes and puts an end to him. / The prophet ends the hard wars of the warring demons, / and exposes that error before the eyes of the onlookers. / For this reason the Lord of creation keeps him, / to show through him the strength of His greatness to the ages to come. / The strength of His greatness the Lord of the prophets revealed to His prophets, / and taught them that He would instruct them through a man. / Through Jeremiah He instructed the world while it was awake, / and as to a yoke He bound it with the yoke of the words of his mouth. / The son of Hilkiah put the wooden yoke on his neck, / and began to plough human thought with the voice of his words. / This is the aim of the ploughing of the diligent ploughman: / the words of the Spirit, which he interpreted in the ears of the people. / The son of Buzi too chose this aim among the Babylonians, / to plough mankind with the voice of divine revelations. / In Babylon the son of the exile received the spirit of revelation, / where the People and the nations thought there was no God. / The divine sign showed him the forms of the chariot, / to which the whole world, the speaking and the mute, was yoked. / The speaking and the mute he saw yoked beneath the Creator, / and the Creator Himself riding high above all. / That chariot which the prophet saw was no chariot, / nor was the running of the wheels beneath it bodily. / They were not wheels that ran outwardly [?], / nor living creatures that possessed the beauty of four faces. / The Spirit drove that chariot which is no chariot, / and spiritually Ezekiel, the skilled seer, saw it. / For the Israelites and the Babylonians he depicted in his vision— / for they supposed that the God of all is not in all places— / that thought and word he overturned by this vision,

to make known that He is over all, and in all, and outside all. / For this reason He depicted likenesses that are not likenesses, / and taught His servant to depict them in the sense of his words. / O divine portion that the son of Buzi received, / and he began to depict the truth of his revelations before the onlookers! / To the whole people he recounted the vision that was shown him, / and charged them not to be divided over what they had heard. / The report of these things Daniel too made them hear, / and he interpreted dreams and rebuked kings to their faces. / Through dreams the Spiritual One taught him kinds of hidden things, / and though they were dreams, they served as the order of prophecy. / With the eye of the spirit of prophecy he saw everything, / and there was nothing in his inquiry that did not come from the Spirit. / The Spirit showed him how to interpret the dreams of the great image, / and at his interpretation the Babylonians [?] and bowed down before him. / By the Spirit he revealed to the tyrant king his humbling, / and turned and instructed him that once humbled he would again be exalted. / By that same Spirit he saw the dissolution of the kingdom of Babylon, / written by a hand of the bodiless Spirit. / It was the Spirit that showed him the vision greater than all visions, / which encompassed the whole world to its end. / He likened the vision shown to him to the great sea, / with four heavenly winds churning it from above. / He saw four beasts coming up out of it, / and the appearance of each differed from the other. / Lion, leopard, and hideous bear he named the three, / and the fourth he did not wish to call by the name of beasts. / Yet it too is a beast, however fearful we may say its appearance was, / for at the beginning he said, “I saw four beasts.” / It was not bodily beasts that the son of the captivity saw, / but figures of the dominion of the nations of the earth. / By the fearful lion he named Babylon, the head of confusion,

and by the name of the leopard he called Cyrus, the head of Persia. / By the bear he represented the kingdom of the Medes, feeble in strength, / and by the fourth the sons of Javan, skilled in mind. / By the great sea he represented the inhabited world, the whole earth, / and by the four winds the heavenly hosts. / To them, the spiritual beings, He apportioned the whole world entire, / and they carry out the service of the four quarters. / By this vision the Spirit instructed the prophet, / and taught him that the kingdoms will pass away and the People return and dwell in the land. / In dreams of the night he saw the vision full of wonder, / and though it was a dream, it is truly the full order of prophecy. / The righteous one was a prophet in exile, humbling kings, / and prophetically he announced the vision of the four beasts. / The Spirit showed him splendid visions in all his visions, / and at the end depicted for him the likeness of our Lord’s death. / The likeness of His death He depicted for the righteous son of the Hebrews, / and called Him by His name: Messiah, who comes to seal the mysteries. / By His death he announced that after His death nothing more remains / to complete the wearisome course of prophecy. / The prophet of the Spirit set a seal upon the revelations, / and sealed them to be guarded until His dawning. / For all that existed among the Hebrews was for His dawning, / and prophets and kings foretold it before it came to be. / Gabriel too, the man of the Spirit, proclaimed His dawning, / and this is the reason he was sent to Daniel. / Daniel, the man of desires, heard the name of Gabriel, / and was greatly amazed at the tidings he heard, which he was not accustomed to. / He had never heard the name of Gabriel at all, / until he heard it from the spiritual one who called him by name. / For this title the righteous one heard was a new name, / and it seems that the course of the law is completed in his name. / The name of Michael belonged to the course of the law, / the one whom even now he called the ruler of the People’s host. / It is he who carried out the governance of the law / from the beginning of the People’s election until the end. / With Hagar the beginning of his service came about,

until that voice addressed to Mary was heard. / An appointed term had been set for him by the Creator, / and he saw that it had drawn near for him to hand his leadership to his fellow. / Gabriel took the leadership of the Israelites / and gave it to the nations, according to the expectation of prophecy. / Through prophecy he showed the prophet his name, “Man,” / so that he would not seem a stranger when he was sent on his mission. / He was to come and bring the good news of our Lord’s dawning, / and it would have been asked what this strange name was. / Had his name not been in the archives of prophecy, / the Israelites would not have received his preaching. / The heralds of the preaching too would have been divided / as to who this Gabriel might be, a stranger by his name. / This division Daniel resolved through prophecy, / and placed the name as a guide at the end of his book. / By this naming of the name Gabriel he trod a way, / so that the course of Michael’s name would cease and his own would enter. / The name Michael is the name of a spiritual angel, / and the name Gabriel is “a man” sent from God. / The name of this man points to this man who cries out from among us [?], / the one whom the righteous one too called “a man” in his preaching. / But what is this naming of name and name, / since they are one and are spirit without composition? / The nature of spiritual beings has no corporeal names, / so why is it that only two have names? / Behold, their ministry reveals the names of their persons, / and though they are one, name is distinct from name. / In the name Michael the severity of punishments is mingled, / and for this reason his title is woven into the book of Moses. / In the name Gabriel, “man,” the title is full of peace, / and Mary bears witness that he brought her the good news full of peace. / The good news of peace Gabriel gave to the one pure of soul, / and though it was new, she received it in faith. / Truly new was the message proclaimed by the spiritual one,

that a virgin should conceive without union or partnership.
By the power of the Spirit he drove the thought from her mind,
he for whom even the things that are hard for nature are easy.
With many proofs he confirmed his word about the conception,
and gave a demonstration from Elizabeth, that she had conceived.
This spiritual man Zechariah had seen,
and it was he who brought him the news of that child, greater than all children.
In the holy temple Zechariah had seen the angel of the Spirit,
and he trembled and was dismayed at the glory upon his face.
“I, I am the man whose name is Gabriel,” he said to him,
“and the Lord has sent me to bring the news of your son’s conception.
Your son is a messenger before the One who comes for the redemption of mankind,
and I have come to reveal that the day of his dawning has arrived.”
With silence he bound him, so that he would not bear witness to anything he had heard
until the plan of the day of his birth was fulfilled.
This was the beginning of the spiritual one’s mission:
that he announced the conception of the herald who goes before the King.
From then on he began to tread the way of our Lord’s dawning,
and by his hand he ministered the visions of the day of his revelation.
It was he who showed the day of his birth to the shepherds,
and he again sounded the voice of his praise among the dwellers of earth.
His are all the things that were spoken in the proclamation,
and it was he who ministered all kinds of revelations to the disciples.
It was he who drew near beside our Savior at the time of the Passion,
and it was he who strengthened his heart, that it not falter at the report of death.
It was he who rolled the great stone from the mouth of the tomb,
and the women saw him standing in the likeness of a man.
He with his companion stood suddenly before the disciples,
and amazed them with the beauty of the glory in which they were clothed.
He ministered all that has been and will be in the proclamation,
just as Michael too ministered in leading the people.
That will which led the people by the hand of Michael
ministered anew its kinds of revelations through Gabriel.
Great is the rank of the spiritual one among the spirits,
as great as his proclamation is beyond all things.

Great, very great is the name of the Messiah beyond all creatures;
therefore great is he who announced his conception, beyond all his companions.
To the greatness of his rank my word has been carried, not idly,
but to make known how glorious was the news he proclaimed.
Glorious is the redemption he proclaimed on earth in the sight of earthly beings,
and heaven and earth bear witness with us that our redemption is great.
At the greatness of his power the hosts on high were amazed,
and they ministered all kinds of his revelations in the sight of his heralds.
The angel of the Spirit chose Philip, one of the seventy,
to go and proclaim the good news of life to one who had no hope.
In the one man whom he turned to faith by his word,
he formed thousands of townsfolk and Cushites.
Here was fulfilled the word our Lord had spoken:
“I have come to cast my teaching among the dwellers of earth.”
Far more than fire did the fire of his proclamation burn,
and it took hold [?] among all the peoples, on sea and on land.
By the might of its greatness it subdued the [?] world,
and humbled the pride of Judaism and of paganism.
In the land of Judah the heralds of the faith prevailed,
and from Jerusalem came the beginning of the word they proclaimed.
By the Spirit of revelation Simon trod the way to the nations,
and cast his net and caught Cornelius first.
A great vision the son of Jonah saw, toward the height:
a sheet coming down in which every kind was gathered.
All the peoples were suspended in that which he saw,
and this is the wonder, that in one sheet he saw everything.
For this vision was a vision of the mind,
and Cephas saw it spiritually and not in the body.
Spiritually he heard the voice: “Rise, kill and eat,”
which taught him that he should not shun sinners.
The unclean peoples he called by the name of the unclean kind,
whom a hidden will was receiving into the household.
Through Cornelius he trod the way of the nations’ turning,
and first fashioned it through the teaching of the head of the disciples.
The angel of the Spirit appeared bodily to a man of the body,
and commanded him to call the man of the body, that he might gain life.

Worthy of wonder is the word the spiritual one spoke,
that through a man he teaches a man, while he himself does not teach.
A great order the angel kept in his mission,
in that he did not approach the lofty rank of leadership.
To the apostles the Lord of the apostles gave the command
to speak the proclamation in the ears of the peoples:
“Go, then, make disciples, baptize and teach among all the peoples,
in the name of the Being: three names, one will.”
That command the spiritual one kept when he was sent:
he spoke the word, but did not choose to complete it by his own ministry.
This is the aim of the mission to mankind:
that through man, men should call man to the proclamation.
The Head of mankind also chose a man,
and through such men sent forth to catch men for the fear of the truth.
With his nets he caught the [?] world,
and brought his catch inside the strongholds of faith.
With this net he caught Paul, the most skilled of fishermen,
and sent him on the way of the proclamation among the nations.
He called him a chosen vessel when he brought him near to apostleship,
and showed that a man can be made perfect in faith.
More than anyone he fulfilled the will of the one who sent him,
and for this he was found worthy of revelations far above him.
It is very lofty for a man to be raised to the [?] of the height,
and yet, very lofty though it was, his paths were completed as it is written.
He said that he went to the place of Eden, which is very far,
and there heard speech that is not heard by human beings.
O wonder that cannot be spoken by any speaker:
that he heard a hearing and spoke a speech that is not spoken!
Tell me, O man: the word your mouth has spoken is difficult,
and no one knows how to recount it before hearers.
But if it is not permitted to speak the words you heard,
how did you hear, or speak, words so difficult?
Very deep is the word, chosen Paul,
and he himself testifies that he could not explain the force of its meaning.
“I know,” he says, “that I went to Eden”—this he recounted—

“but I do not know how I went, only that I went.
That I went, and only that, the Spirit revealed to me spiritually,
but my mind could not search out the way by which I went.”
Let us say, then, to anyone who speaks of Paul’s word,
saying that he did not know: it is presumption to dispute with him.
It is presumption to search out words that cannot be spoken,
especially since no one is permitted to hear them.
The nature of mortals is not permitted to hear them
until it becomes immortal; then it will hear them.
A new thing it was in that man who spoke them,
and rightly he said that he spoke and heard in no ordinary way.
In no ordinary way he heard the speech that cannot be spoken;
so it is plain that he passed beyond the order of mortality.
Paul alone chose to become like the immortals,
and he bears witness to the power that empowered him to accomplish these things.
For it is the power of the Creator to make something out of nothing,
and to raise his servants above anything that can be spoken.
It is he who taught all kinds of his wisdom to the members of his household,
and interpreted what is too hard for hearing to put into speech.
His power strengthened the weakness of the human mind,
and led the world by glories it had not seen.
Glorious indeed were the words the apostles spoke on earth,
and no one knows how to recount the force of their meanings.
Wisely he accomplished all that he accomplished, making man wise,
and bound all in perfect love with the Lord of all.
This aim, which brings peace to all, my thoughts have called to mind,
and I mingle its story with the story of the divine visions.
For his sake, too, were the visions the righteous saw,
and like guides they trod the way to the day of his revelation.
The day of his revelation brought to rest the course of all revelations,
and bound mankind and the heavenly beings in peace with him.
In the peace that is with him a door was opened between him and all,
and nothing remained that was not reconciled with the Creator.
Through a son of man the Lover of mankind accomplished this,

and through him he removed the barrier and abolished death and the [?].
Through him he promised life without death to mortal nature,
and raised it up in the true hope of the coming day of resurrection.
He knew that the life of time is worn out in its course,
and he prepared beforehand another life, restful and peaceful.
He was well aware that the nature of mortals is worn down by mortality,
and he hastened to loose the yoke of death from it.
This was manifest to him, which he accomplished in the fullness of times,
and he revealed it beforehand through the revelations he revealed to his servants.
The saints were like guides going before his will,
and they trod the way by which to lead mankind toward his will.
See, O man, how greatly he loves the race of mankind,
that in nature itself he shows the love of his goodness.
His love he showed through visions of many different likenesses,
and he brought them to their close in the one likeness of one son of man.
One son of man he chose from all the nature of mortals,
and called him by his own name and gave him the rank of his divinity.
See, O son of man, how high the All-Bountiful has raised you,
that he took what is yours and gave you what is his, in love.
Glorious is the will that called him by the name of its glories,
and too small is the mouth of all creation to give thanks with us.
The debt of love that is upon us cannot be repaid;
can the eloquent or the mute recount the kinds of his greatness?
He alone is sufficient to pay the price of our redemption,
since he knows of us that our race is too poor to repay.
It is not repayment he seeks from us, he who has no need,
but to teach us that when we repay we shall rejoice in our measure.
He teaches us as he urges us on to repayment,
and this is out of love, and not to fill any need of his own.
Worthy of praise from every mouth, glorious in his being,
his glory in itself urges his servants to glorify him.
Response: Blessed is he who exalted his servants by his revelation,
and made them temples for his greatness.
On the Revelations to Abraham

The Third Homily
For the Fourth Sunday of the Annunciation
On the Revelations to Abraham

The Lord of creation chose one people to be his own,
and through it he taught all the peoples the power of his greatness.
He left all the peoples to the freedom he had set in nature,
and kept for himself one inheritance through his revelations.
He set on them the seal of his name and marked them,
so that they would not mingle with the tribes and stray from his name.
He surrounded them with the law of his words like a wall,
and bound them with commandments as with a rope.
He chose a dwelling for himself in the people he had chosen as his own,
to teach them how much he loves the children of his house.
He urged them on by means of sacrifices of flesh and blood,
so that they would offer him sacrifices of love, as to the Hidden One.
He honored them in the eyes of the tribes by the power of his help,
and exalted them above the peoples by the victory of his might.
He showed that he is just by chastising them when they sinned,
and proclaimed his power through the victories he gave in battle.
For all the peoples he ordained and set up rulers,
but the people he chose he led in his own name.
It was not out of malice that he rejected the peoples and chose a people;
rather, in the people he chose he arranged beforehand what was to come.
Through one people he willed to make all the peoples wise,
for by his own command he made all things, and in him all things stand.
Like the foundation at the beginning of a house he laid down the people,

and on it he completed the building of the peoples, as it pleased him.
He planted Abraham among the peoples like a root,
and nurtured his soul through divine revelations.
He cut a shoot from a tree bitter in its nature,
and transplanted it, and its branches bore fruits of glory.
From paganism, bare of spiritual fruits,
Abram's love blossomed as a fruit full of sweetness.
Of his own accord he offered firstfruits and gave him a voice of praise,
and as a firstfruit he offered the [?] of his faith.
The Creator's power beckoned him and drew him out of Babylon,
to leave his place and go to dwell in a foreign land.
This the One who knows all revealed to him in mystery:
"Leave your error and come, be enlightened by the light of my knowledge.
Release your will from the chains of carved idols and sorceries,
and I will give you freedom of soul to know whom you should worship.
Leave the inheritance of your fathers' house, full of thorns,
and I will gain for you an inheritance of love toward my lordship."
It did not grieve him to leave his place and forsake his people,
nor did he trouble himself over why he should go to another land.
The name of exile, full of troubles, did not distress him,
nor did the lovelessness of the house of strangers grieve him.
He set out from his place on a road full of sufferings and pains,
and with his limbs his thoughts set out after his Lord.
He became a stranger to the kinship of the children of his people,
and loved and cherished belonging to the household of his Lord.
He went out from Babylon, the spring that poured out the lore of the Chaldeans,
and dwelt in Harran, the mother that gave birth to sorcery.
The purity of his soul was not muddied by the divinations of Babylon,
nor was his faith shaken by the sorceries of Harran.
The will of his love did not change with the change of place,
nor was he drawn by any excuse into the worship of images.
The place did not weaken his righteousness;
by the will of his love it only strengthened his faith.
His body was bare of fleshly offspring,
yet at all times he brought forth fruits of glory in his mind.

Barrenness of the flesh was the companion of him and of Sarah,
yet at all times their thoughts yielded a voice of praise.
His Lord tested him through barrenness as through fire,
and showed his beauty through praise without doubting.
It was not that he had to learn it, for he knew him before he was formed;
but to the generations to come he revealed the strength of their faith.
He moved him on to sojourn in the house of strangers,
to sow love and faith in a barren land.
He left Harran to go to the land promised to him,
to cast there the fire of his love and set the forest ablaze.
He went out rejoicing in the promise of his Lord, who does not lie,
and beyond hope he believed in hope that he would inherit the land.
The righteous man set out on the terms of the land promised to him,
and he believed and trusted that his seed would be full of nations.
He became a sojourner in the land he had received in a promise,
and as a stranger he dwelt in the place pledged to him.
He multiplied his labor in the land of the Canaanites through revelations,
and yielded fruits of hope and love and faith.
Every day he heard the voice: "Your seed will inherit the land,"
and there was no heir, yet he trusted the voice with nothing yet fulfilled.
"Lift up your eyes and look to the heavens, at the sparks of light,
and count the sand on the seashore, if you can.
So shall the child of your body multiply," the voice called to him,
"and your seed shall be beyond number, as I have said.
Stretch out your thoughts to the four corners and look at the lands
which your seed will subdue in one [?].
By myself I have sworn, and I do not lie in my hidden nature,
that in you the peoples of the earth shall be blessed through faith.
Because you stripped off the hateful garment of the name of paganism,
by your faith I will cover with it the shame of the peoples.
Because you trod the path by confessing one Creator,
for the sake of your love I draw all to faith in me.

"Because by your will you opened the door to my hidden lordship,
through you I open the door of life to those dead in iniquity.
Because you did not doubt my promises while they were far off,
I make you a head of life in the kingdom on high.
Because my lordship dawned in your mind, hidden though I am,
from you shall dawn the One who gathers the peoples into one.
In return for exile in places full of troubles,
I make you a haven of peace for all who are distressed.
Upon you I build the building of love and faith,
and through you I strengthen all the peoples with the hope of life."
The One who knows all tested the upright man through promises;
he believed in things far off as though they were near.
And knowing that he would not waver concerning his promises,
he revealed the truth of his faith through trial.
He knew before he tested him that his love was true,
but he sought an occasion to proclaim him as one who does not waver.
He willed to urge on the children of his race by his conduct,
and wrote them in the book of his words, so that they might become like him.
Like an image he painted the beauty of his faith,
so that each might fix its strength in his own mind.
His body was dry through barrenness as through thirst,
but his soul was watered with the drink of the Spirit and bore fruit.
He told him, "To your seed I give the land of Canaan,"
yet drove him out of it as an exile to the land of Egypt.
He raised the rod and struck the land with a severe famine,
so that he would flee from it because of the famine to another place.
He tested him greatly by changes of place,
so that all might hear that he did not falter before troubles.
He fled from the famine to save his life in the land of Egypt,
and they cut off his other half and snatched from him the rib that clung to him.
He did not murmur that wicked men had taken the land of his seed,
nor did he waver when they took from him the [?] of his fruits.

He was certain that the voice that called him does not lie,
and that no other would come near the land that clung to him, to cling to it.
He grew rich in that land and [?] greatly in his priesthood,
and the wealth of his faith prevailed over earthly things.
He dwelt in a region where demons were served by sorcery,
and the fruits of his faith shone in glory among the tares.
O tree that nurtured itself in the midst of thorns,
and with the branches of its love beat down the fruits of the wicked!
O sojourner who went into exile among strangers,
and kings and free men bowed before him against their will!
O stranger who came to supply the needs of his life,
and raised the rod and struck the people of the place!
The Lord struck Pharaoh the king and his household
because of Sarah, Abram's wife, whom he had snatched from him.
And while he was swept along with the world by the needs of his possessions,
his wronged wealth was increasing by his Lord's command.
His honor grew because of Sarah, whom the king had taken,
and he thanked his Lord, who gave him wealth through these occasions.
The wise man grew rich in a land poor in knowledge,
and loaded up his wealth to go to the land promised to him.
He returned and dwelt in the land of Canaan as though it were his own,
looking to the promise of his Lord, who was giving it to him.
The number of the years of his life reached ninety-nine,
and he spoke with him through a revelation, that he should circumcise his flesh.
The servant fell on his face and bowed down before his Maker,
and he established a covenant with him, that he would mark his seed with his name.
He changed his name, by which he had been called as of a single people,
and called him by a name that means "father of the peoples."
With the change by which he changed it and called him father of the peoples,
the voice called to him: "From now on receive the child I promised.
"Behold, the promise made before you is fulfilled in deeds,
and I give you a son out of grace, beyond the order of nature.
Behold, I bring your dead body to life and it gives seed,
and I make a shoot sprout from a root that has grown old and worn out.

I comfort barren Sarah out of her barrenness,
and make the shamed woman bold through the fruit that comes from her.
I take away the reproach from her body, the name of barrenness,
and give her a child as a reward for her strength."
The promises were fulfilled and the pledges to the barren were made good,
for the Hidden One came to give a choice reward to the righteous.
The Lord revealed himself to Abram in the land of Mamre,
as he sat at the door of his house in the heat of the day.
O fervent man, whom the harshness of the heat did not weigh down,
who scorned rest lest he fall short in his hospitality!
He raised his eyes, looking over the roads,
that he might complete his love by feeding the needy.
Abraham saw a new vision, full of wonder:
three watchers clothed in human form.
He ran rejoicing, fell down and bowed before the spiritual beings,
and begged them to complete his love by resting with him.
Before them he called on the Creator's name through revelations:
"Do not, my Lord, pass by the house of your servant who waits for you."
O Being hidden from all and invisible,
who revealed himself to Abraham in human form!
O righteous man who was worthy to see in mystery
the Word of the Father, who was to put on a human body!
Three entered Abraham's house in outward form,
and Abraham spoke with one alone, as with God.
The Word of the Father put on a likeness in mystery,
and Abram rejoiced that he saw the Hidden One in a chosen body.
He gave a welcome to the Lord and the servants according to what he saw,

and refreshed them with bread and water, as he saw fit.
And the spiritual beings too acted before him in keeping with his welcome,
appearing to eat, though they did not eat, for the sake of his love.
It is not in the nature of spiritual beings to take food,
nor are heavenly beings nourished by earthly things.
For Abram's love they condescended to food and appeared to eat,
yet they remained without nourishment, as is well known.
The Lord and the servants accepted the love of the good servant,
and repaid him with the reward of conception and a child beyond nature.
"At this season I will return to you," he said to him,
"and barren Sarah shall have fruit while she is still alive."
He accepted his love and gave recompense in the announcement of conception,
and revealed and laid out the punishment of the wicked who trampled his ordinances:
"The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah has come up before me;
I will go down and see whether the deed is as the report."
O Knower of all, who in his love bore the hardness of our race,
who, knowing the wickedness of our inclination, holds back his wrath!
He revealed to Abram that he would rain fire on the insolent,
and showed that he is merciful: if there were righteous men, he would put away his wrath.
Abraham saw his Lord's will, that he loves to forgive,
and he asked and entreated him to turn from his anger.
He humbled himself before his Maker in his supplication,
for he saw that his own nature was too small to plead for forgiveness.
He accepted from him the supplication of his love as he pleaded:
"If there are righteous men, I will not destroy the place in wrath."
Abram asked, "If there are fifty, will you spare the place?"
And the Gentle One came down with him as far as ten.
"If there are ten righteous in Sodom, I will spare it,"
and though he knew there was only one, he said, "if there are."
The spiritual beings set out from Abram and came to Sodom,
and Abram's kinsman received them in the manner of Abram.
The men of flesh ran wild with lust after the spiritual beings,
for they saw them clothed in flaming radiance.
On this condition the One who knows all sent them:
that they might be witnesses to the wickedness of men who had corrupted order.
And though nature had committed great infamy and corrupted its way,
did not the Good One mingle mercy with his anger when he judged them?

With fire he struck down the frenzy of the lust of the debauched,
and made the place a showing of the wickedness of the men who had grown insolent.
He rescued the righteous man from destruction with the wicked,
and showed his mercy in that he was saved, for he is a lover of mankind.
Abraham rejoiced to see the Hidden One through his revelations,
and though he was dust, he was worthy to speak with the Being.
His Lord accepted the supplication of his love for Lot, who was saved,
and comforted him and gave him the reward of conception and a child.
The promises were fulfilled and the pledges made good, and Sarah conceived,
and bore a child beyond the order set in nature.
The righteous who had waited for the payment of the reward received the reward,
and gave thanks to the voice that had watered their limbs.
In Isaac the barren righteous ones received their promises,
and rejoiced to see in what was near the thing that was far off.
With one figure the One who knows all comforted them,
and showed them in mystery what was to come.
In return for the will with which they [?] him as their lord,
he made them worthy to see the mystery of the hope of the peoples.
He gave recompense to their hospitable wills:
that from them would dawn the One who multiplies hope for the hopeless.
They rejoiced and were comforted, for they saw a hope that does not lie,
which the One who promised gave them sealed with oaths.
Even the beginning of the fulfillment of the mysteries for the righteous
he sealed, saying, "Abram saw me and rejoiced in hope."
With the child Isaac he comforted them out of barrenness,
and brought them as into a furnace in the mystery of his sacrifice.
The Lord called, "Abram, Abram!" through a revelation:
"Take your only son and offer him up to me as a burnt offering on the mountain.
A new sacrifice I ask of you to offer me,
for I know your love for me, that it does not lie."
The good servant did not delay at his Lord's command,
nor did he murmur that he was overturning the hope of his own promise.
The father rose early the next day, as he had been commanded,
and with a pure heart prepared the wood for burning his son.
For three days the voice drew him on to travel the road,
and the righteous man's love did not waver from its readiness.

He revealed and showed him the place of the sacrifice to which he had called him,
and he left his servants and led his son, as he willed.
He took the knife, the fire and the wood to prepare the sacrifice,
and did not reveal the mystery of Isaac's slaying to his household.
The servants stayed at the foot of the mountain on this understanding:
that he would go up to worship with the boy and then come back.
The sacrifice spoke with its sacrificer, the child with his father:
"Here are the fire and the wood; where is the lamb for the sacrifice?"
The father gave his only son an answer of hope:
"God will see to it and prepare a lamb for the sacrifice."
He comforted his son with the hope of his Lord, so that it would not grieve him,
and he in turn accepted his father's word without doubting.
He built the altar, laid out the wood and bound him for the sacrifice;
with his own will he drew the knife to slaughter his son.
O mind whose love wrestled with the limbs,
and loosed the love of its kinship in the love of its Lord!
O nature clothed in the grief of the sufferings of the flesh,
which, when the pangs of compassion struck it, defied its own nature!
O athlete who waged a contest with himself,
and overcame the sufferings of the body by the strength of his mind!
The heavenly beings marveled at the strength of soul of the new priest,
who held back his compassion to bind his love in the love of his Lord.
He raised the knife to slaughter his son without hesitation,
and the voice stopped him: "I do not want a human sacrifice."
The Lord called, "Abram, Abram," and spoke with him:
"Hold back your hand from your heir and do not harm him.
I accept your sacrifice together with your will, as though he had been sacrificed,
for you have made known your love for me before the eyes of the spiritual beings.
Because you listened and did not delay at my command to you,
your seed shall be like the sand on the seashore.
Because you did not withhold your son from the knife, to be a sacrifice,
I have sworn by my nature to pour out my blessings on your descendants.
In return for the offering your hands offered with a whole heart,
through you I bind up the peace that was torn by the transgression of the commandment.
It was not a human sacrifice I wanted you to offer me;

what is to come I wished to reveal through you in this that you have done.
By a human sacrifice I am about to bind up the peace of all,
and beforehand I portrayed in your son's sacrifice the death of my Beloved.
If your son dies, he does not pay the debt of his race;
my Son, who is from your seed, by his death undoes the dominion of death.
One from your seed I take in the fullness of times,
and I make him a perfect sacrifice that atones for all.
In Isaac's death I sketched the death of the One who [?] died,
who will also die, yet whose body will not decay in Sheol.
In the binding of Isaac's hands I portrayed the nails in his hands:
here in mystery, and there in truth, in deeds.
Love and compassion for his Lord bound Isaac,
and love and compassion for his race bind him.
In Isaac you fulfilled love and compassion toward my lordship,
and in him I show riches and love toward all.
In Isaac I depict a figure of his death and the resurrection of his life,
for I raise him up after his death, and he does not decay.
For Isaac the ram was the ransom, by the command,
but he is ransomed by the hidden power that dwells in him.
I have made you, Abram, a head of life, here and there;
in the mystery of truth I fulfill for him the promise made before you.
Behold, I have shown you the mystery of salvation in your son's sacrifice:
that One I sacrifice in the fullness of times for the salvation of all.
Behold, I have given you a ram as a sacrifice; complete your will:
release the speaking one, slaughter the silent one, and complete your sacrifice.
See, Abraham, that I have given a reward for your love toward me,
for I have revealed and shown you the mystery hidden from the heavenly beings:
that your seed, Abram, I am about to put on like a garment,
so that in its revealing it may proclaim the power of my only Son.

By my will I dwell in the firstfruit of your seed,
and before the door of his body all will worship my nature.
Behold, I have accepted the sacrifice of your hands together with your will;
go down, seeing the fulfillment of your sacrifice: it is the salvation of the peoples."
Abram raised his eyes and saw a ram on the mountain,
which a sign had bound at the top of a tree for the deliverance of his child.
He completed his will and finished his sacrifice with the ram,
and rejoiced to see the truth in the mystery his hands had served.
With this hope the Good One gladdened the righteous,
and made them the head of the order of the kingdom on high.
In them he made a promise to all who are invited to share their way of life:
that, as in a haven, he gives rest in their presence to those who have toiled.
He honored them through promises yet to come,
and drew the image of their way of life for the generations to come.
He invited the peoples from the four corners to their bridal chambers,
to come and rejoice spiritually at their tables.
Abraham was worthy to be the head in the kingdom on high,
for by his faith he trod the path for the turning of the peoples.
His confession became like the foundation at the beginning of a house,
and in it love, hope and faith were brought to completion.
Because the righteous man endured his body's barrenness and did not waver,
he made him father to the peoples who resemble him in his faith.
Let Abram be like a mirror through his way of life,
and let us see ourselves in it, lest we be found hateful through hidden iniquity.
Let us sow hope and love in the land of his faith,
and reap spiritual fruits without end.
In him let the barren, bare of promise, be comforted,
and obtain a child beyond hope, in his likeness.
In the company of his love let them travel the narrow paths of this life,
so that it may be for them a haven of rest from their troubles.
After the pattern of his wealth let the rich too acquire wealth,
and be heirs with him in the wealth on high.
Let those who possess earthly treasures become like him,
and acquire with him heavenly treasures that are not dissolved.
Let his beauty be like a mirror for all who see it,
and let them acquire love for the poor by providing for them in their time.

Let rich women who have acquired much look to Sarah,
who, though she had possessions in her hands, served the spiritual beings.
Let her humility of soul strike down the rich women,
for she did not exchange Abram's love for the wealth of Egypt.
Let her accuse, by the strength of her faith alone,
the foolish women who ask unclean demons for a child.
Let the length of her years rebuke the adulterous women,
for after so many years she received a child beyond hope.
Let Sarah be like a mirror for the daughters of Eve,
and let them look into her and not doubt the Creator.
In Abram let the lovers of wealth see themselves,
he who managed his wealth and humbled himself like a poor man.
Let the righteous, by their way of life, be open images,
and let each one paint the image of their beauty in his mind.
With the love of our souls let us bind our love to the Creator,
so that he may give a reward for our faith together with his true ones.
On the Nativity of Our Lord

The Third Homily on the Nativity of Our Lord.
Response:
Blessed is Christ, who on the day of his birth
gladdened the earth and made heaven rejoice.
My brothers

In love and mercy the Creator willed to give life to all,
and He sent His Son to turn all to the knowledge of Him.
The Word of the Father went forth from the Father without changing,
and came to our dwelling, while He was with us and in all.
His will went forth and came in His love to the earthly ones,
and His nature remained without alteration in what He was.
Not in nature did God, the All, go forth or change,
for Being has no [?] by which to go forth among its creations.
For He does not go forth by change from what He is,
since in what He is He remains forever without alteration.
He showed His love to the human race by this, that He came,
to magnify greatly the name of His salvation before their eyes.
He honored the lowliness of Adam's dwelling by coming down,
for if Being comes down to it, how much greater is it than all!
For the ruin of His image He willed to come down in a child's stature,
to cast it again in the furnace of the Spirit and renew it.
With the name of Being He named the dust of the son of the mire,
and what had fallen and been corrupted He came down and raised from the mire.
He named His image with a borrowed stature, according to His greatness,
for all that was made by Being is far inferior.
Exalted is His nature above the things made, beyond measure,
and it has no visible image like the earthly ones.
He magnified His image with the name of image, that He might bind all in it,
so that they might gain love for knowledge of Him through the name of His image.
In the honor of His image the Fashioner of all gave all a share,
and by its free will He taught them to hate iniquity.

Through redemption He tested His image, as in a furnace,
and showed the beauty of its reason through trial.
The envious one saw the greatness of the rank of Adam's image;
he conceived iniquity and brought forth guile against the blameless one.
The envious one filled the bow of wrath with the arrow of guile;
he struck him and shot at him the hard arrow of desire for the fruit.
By cunning he swept away the image of the name of Being,
and by his wiles he loosed the love that keeps all in its place.
He troubled the peace of brotherhood with a rain of iniquity,
and cut off the road by which men journey toward the Hidden One.
The rational and the dumb became strangers to the human race,
and they gave up hope over his fall, that he would never rise again.
The unclean demons rejoiced and laughed at his fall,
and the foul ones danced to see the abasement of him who was honored above all.
And when the Good One saw the contempt for His image and the boasting of the wicked,
He took pity on His image, that it should not be mocked by the insolent.
His love drew Him to compassion, to fashion His image anew,
so that the power of His wisdom should not come to nothing with its ruin.
He knew before its making that the sinner would sin,
and as one who knows, His love went ahead of it toward forgiveness.
In this, that it was being tested, justice was weighing the matter,
and He did not by repentance cut off the menace of the way of death:

For this reason the Hidden One came to us in the revealed,
and in our kinsman He rendered to us the power of His [?].
His will went forth and came to His own, to visit His own;
as befits the Boundless One in visiting His own,
He sent His will by a spiritual messenger.
And the Watcher proclaimed new words in the ears of flesh;
with a sign of peace His will sowed in the earth of flesh,
to uproot error and sow hope for one who had no hope.
The Watcher gave greeting to Mary at the beginning of his words,
to loose the bonds of that daughter of the voice that pronounced judgment.
A pure greeting with grace he gave to the pure one,
to wash away the bitterness the evil one sowed in Eve's ears:
"Peace to you, Mary, of the race of Eve, whom death had marked out,
for the fruit from you looses the bonds of mortality.
Peace to you, woman, a creature of flesh, of human build,
for the King has willed to [?] an image within your members.
By the power of the Spirit He has willed to build a temple; await it!
That it may be a dwelling, and He may dwell in it by His will;
for no drugs paint Him on the page of your body.
That through it He may make known the authority of His hidden Begetter,
He shall be great, and holy, and glorious above all.
He takes the rank and the great name of the name of Being;
to Him shall be given the headship of David's throne.
And He shall reign over all, He who does not hand His crown to others."
Let the sons of strife come now, those clothed in boasting,
and show us to whom the Watcher's words belong.
Let Eutyches, worker of falsehood, arise with his disciples,
and explain to us whose is the conception that is by the Spirit.
Let the [?] Egyptian apostle come with him too,
and show us who it is that took David's throne.
Let the insolent of our days arise with them,
and show us who it is that reigns over the house of Jacob.
Arise, Egyptian, at the head of the camp of your party,
and array the ranks of your forces to meet the truth;
at you above all the target of our word is aimed.
For you, more than anyone, confused the right order;
from you sprang the hateful word of passibility.
For you confined the Boundless One within members;
like a buckler of the heretics you turn against us [?].
For whose is the conception the Watcher proclaimed in Mary's ears?
If it is the Word who lowered Himself to become flesh,
what was it that compelled the Spirit to come and complete His conception?
Why did He not compound Himself in the womb,
so that the Spirit and the Power of the Father came down, and so He was compounded?
When did He give up the name of Being that is with His Begetter,
that now He is given the exalted name of holiness?
Reveal and explain to us the hidden mysteries of your secrets:
how did the Spirit form the Word of the Father in the womb?
How did the Spirit give body to the formless Spirit?
And how did a small bosom hold Him who holds all?
How did it cut short the eternity of Him who has no beginning?

And did He begin to be a new becoming, not by His will?
Whose is the flesh that the Spirit compounded within members?
Is the flesh His own, or is it from Mary's body?
Did He change Himself into flesh by what is His, or by what is ours?
Reveal and make it plain to us, that we may know at what target you aim in your amazement.
If it was His own nature that became flesh in the womb,
then where is the fulfillment of His words to David?
And if He is flesh that He compounded by His own power,
then what is His remains in what is His, without change.
But if He changed Himself into what is His or into another,
then He possessed Being in name and not in deeds;
there is no time that cuts off the eternity of Being.
And if it is cut off, it is not Being but belongs to time;
far be it from us to say this, like the wicked.
Rather, let us confess that all Being is without end;
for neither height nor depth, nor all that is in them,
can shake the edifice of the word of our soul's [?].
Let there be no other hope for us in which to glory,
but in this: that the Word was not diminished in our body;
let the rational and the dumb cry out with us, with voice and with silence.
For the Word of the Father remains unchangeably in what is His;
His nature did not change and become despised flesh.
Rather, He took flesh from what is ours and honored it in what is His;
His own nature remains in His glory without alteration.
And what is ours, which He took, He made one with Himself in honor;
He who is hidden from all did not come to become flesh.
He compounded flesh so that through it He might make known His hiddenness;
the Spirit is able to compound humans from a daughter of men.
That men might see in His inner being Him who is hidden from all,
and that no drugs of human seed formed Him in the womb,
so that His conception should rise above the order of His fellows,
by the Spirit He was fashioned, and the Spirit filled Him with the power of His will.
That from His fullness He might grant life and give life to [?],
He made Him perfect and well-tempered in body and soul,
that through Him He might set body and soul free from servitude;
as a firstfruit the Fashioner of all chose Him from all,
that through Him He might grant life without end to [?].
The spiritual beings rejoiced at the new voice announcing His conception,
and began to aim at the target of peace toward men.
Gabriel sowed [?] tidings in Mary's ears,
a new conception, not by the nature of human seed;
the [?] virgin carried the fruit whose seed was a voice.
And the spirit sang on the lyre of its soul a song of praise;
with a song of thanksgiving she paid the wage of the new conception:
"Blessed is He who chose for His love a dwelling within my members,
the Fashioner of all, who is worthy of praise from all mouths!
For in my humility He willed to exalt the dust of Adam."
In the first month Gabriel sowed a conception in her ears,
and the ear of the bread of life sprang up wondrously;
he gave her to taste the power of life in the foundation of her body,
and in the month of Kanun she bore a cluster that gladdens all:

At the time when the earth conceived Adam the firstborn in the beginning,
in it Adam was compounded, who was moistened in the earth [?].
One spiritual being was messenger at the announcing of His conception,
and on the day of His birth many came down and shouted praise.
The Watcher gave Mary a sign to confirm her conception:
"The fruit that makes bodies flourish, dwellings that had grown old and worn out—
behold, Elizabeth too has conceived beyond expectation.
And this is the sixth month in the count of her conception:
the messenger is conceived before the King, beyond expectation."
And a King was conceived outside the order of marriage;
Mary carried a great treasure within her members.
And she went out to learn the Watcher's words by experience;
a ship laden with wealth came into the house of the poor.
Suddenly the barren womb was made rich at the sound of her words;
the daughter of the King gave greeting to the mother of the servant.
And the babe began to leap in the womb to meet his Lord.
O wombs, from whose wombs comfort was won!
O mothers, who were made wise by their babes!
The barren one bore the voice of the [?] who proclaims hope;
the virgin bore the fulfillment of the mystery and the [?] of the peoples.
The herald heard the voice of the mother of the King of kings,
and rejoiced to meet her, and rejoiced in his mother by the spirit of revelation.
The barren one hastened to meet the conception of virginity,
and answered and said: "Blessed is your child above all children!
Who has granted the bearer of treasure to come in to her?
A woman has been made worthy to become the mother of the Lord of all."
Mary heard the confirmation of the spiritual one's words,
and gained an undivided hope in her mind;
she returned home with the gift with which she was laden.
And she waited for when she would see the hope revealed;
nine months she hid her wealth in the ship of her body,
until she came to rest in the harbor of childbirth, in the order of infants.
She sailed through the waves of slander from the insolent,
until she came to rest within Bethlehem, as was expected.
A decree went out from Augustus, king of the peoples,
that every man should enroll himself in his own place for the poll-tax.
Joseph too went up to the land of Judah, to the city of David,
and he led his betrothed with him, as the decree required.
The decree of the earthly king gathered people together,
that he might [?] them under the authority of his headship;
the decree of the poll-tax became the cause of life.
And he enrolled them, the children of men, in a deed of freedom;
through the king's occasion, the world heard of the King who dawned in Judah.
And people began to enroll the deed of their life in His name;
a hidden sign drew the king of the earth to the decree,
that through it the headship of the kingdom on high might be revealed.
In the city of David the promises made to David were fulfilled,
and the course of prophecy too came to rest within Bethlehem;
the birth pangs pressed upon the ship laden with the wealth of all.

And she opened the treasury before spiritual and bodily beings;
a hidden sign gathered the heavenly ones.
They came down and proclaimed good hope to the hopeless;
their voices became like trumpets, and they proclaimed on earth:
"Arise, you who were sunk down, and shake off the yoke that iniquity laid on you;
the spiritual beings have gained hope for the bodily ones on your account.
Come, freely receive the deed of their debts through the King who has dawned!"
To the shepherds they revealed the mystery of Him who shepherds all,
and truth taught them, revealed in the Babe and His mother.
The bodily heard from the spiritual the promise of life,
and the voice of promise gathered them to the deed.
To the household the spiritual ones were sent, and roused them;
and to the outsiders He sent His sign and gathered them.
The sons of the house He confirmed through the promise,
and those far off He encouraged by a star of light.
With the insiders He spoke through those who speak,
and to the outsiders He made Himself heard through silent things;
He sent a star as a messenger after the peoples,
that they might come and see the salvation of life among the peoples.
Mystically He spoke with them in the stirrings of the soul,
and by a sign of light He showed them the way of life;
by the very thing in which they erred He made them wise to learn the truth.
The things they worshipped He made a guide before the worshippers,
for in Chaldean lore the erring had gone astray and brought in the fates,
and had made the luminaries lords of death and life;
to the star they had given headship and subjection.
So He subjected them to His lordship in the very thing they practiced:
the vision of light showed them the children of their error.
For one of the Watchers ran with it before their eyes;
it was no natural thing hung in the firmament that came down to them,
but a sign that showed itself in a star of light.
One spiritual being carried the sign that was given to him,
and made it shine like a luminary for the children of darkness.
And that in truth it was not a natural working,
its course bears witness, for it differed from the luminaries;
it alone changed the order of the dance of its path.
And it lowered its height toward the earthly ones, that they might examine it;
its appearance and its course were constantly before their eyes,
until they entered the land of Judah, and its light was hidden.
To the house of strangers it showed its light and the course of its path,
but toward the household it drew in its rays and hid its light;
it was not its own to run, or to stay from its journey.
The sign hid it from their eyes at the appointed time;
He willed to rebuke the circumcised people by the uncircumcised peoples.
For while strangers sought the King as though they were of the household,
the uncircumcised in flesh asked the uncircumcised in mind:
"Where is the King who has been born in Judah, as was expected?
The star of light has revealed and shown us His birth.

And it has drawn us to Him, that we might turn to Him the worship of love."
The household saw the children of their error seeking the truth,
and though unwilling, they recounted the proof of prophecy.
For this reason He made the revelation to those far off,
that they might come and be chosen witnesses against the wicked;
the outsiders cried out to the household and roused them.
And the sunken ones leapt at the sound of the remembrance of the books of the Spirit.
The king too heard the report of the King; he trembled and was dismayed,
lest the appointed term of prophecy had been fulfilled.
The report of the King fell on the ears of the Edomite,
and that the decree of Jacob's words was already fulfilled;
the proselyte heard that a King was arising from the house of the dead [?].
And a groan seized him, for the words were coming close to fulfillment in deeds;
the cunning fox saw the tracks of the lion's whelp.
And he began to creep into the [?] of guile to hide himself;
he called the magi and questioned them in the guise of love:
at what time had they seen the appearance of the King's star?
He put on the guise of wishing to worship, and asked about this,
and whetted a sword in his mind to shed blood.
The Chaldeans heard the fulfillment of the words of all creatures,
and did not discern the scheme that was hidden in his mind;
the innocent went out in simplicity from the king's presence.
And the guide that had left them rose before their eyes,
and with its light comfort too dawned in their minds.
And the hidden sign that drew them to worship the King
made them aware of the guile the king had forged in secret;
it taught them also the wiles of which the guile was compounded.
They went on while the light of the sign ran before their eyes,
until it came and set them at the King's door.
The messengers whom the Hidden One had sent entered the house of the earthly ones,
and they saw the King in a despised dwelling, and were not divided in doubt.
O command, which strengthens divided impulses!
And they were not weakened by the divisions of hesitation;
the Chaldeans kept a great order in their minds,
for they did not ask where were the crown and the authority of the King.
The sign put bridles of silence on the stirrings of the soul,
and set them in order, that they should not stumble through division;
they ran calmly under that guidance.
And they honored the body that is upon the chariot on which the King rides;
they revered and worshipped the Hidden One in the Revealed, who was despised to sight.
And in the Bodily One they saw the spiritual, with the stirrings of the soul;
they opened the treasures with which their proofs were laden.
And they offered them and revealed the power of their meanings:
with gold they showed His authority, who reigns over all
and exacts from all the poll-tax of the mouth's thanksgiving;
with myrrh they showed that He would suffer hereafter as a man,
and thus be exalted above death by the power of Him who assumed Him:

With frankincense they revealed the power of the hiddenness of Him who is hidden from all.
And to Him the rational and the dumb owe the worship of love;
they gave Him gold as to the King who rules over all.
And they offered myrrh, which greatly relieves the sufferings of the body;
frankincense they paid as thanksgiving from His creatures.
By a manifest sign they gave Him glory that profits above all;
in three gifts they bounded and held all offerings.
And each one of them by its own showed His authority;
three offered three sacrifices in the temple of the King.
And they were the first to proclaim the Trinity, hidden from all;
they completed the course of the preaching of their offerings.
And He taught them through revelations another way.
Herod saw that the Assyrians had greatly mocked him,
and he poured out his wrath on the children without pity;
with the sword against the children he [?] the babes who were hemming him in.
On the Babe who, he heard, would take his crown and reign over all,
he was exacting the vengeance of death from the children.
For this reason he takes vengeance on the children,
that with them He who is [?] might perish.
He gave the order, and the Edomite was mad to shed blood;
he raised his sword over the camp of the ranks of Jacob.
The weeping of babes was heard in the land of Judah,
and womanhood was set aflame with the sound of lament;
Rachel wept and could not be comforted in her grief,
for she saw her sons slaughtered unjustly.
Weeping and wailing filled the streets of the city of David.
While these mothers were mourning over their babes,
the babes became hostages of peace through their slaying.
And the King received them in love as a firstfruit;
the death of time cut their life short of its fulfillment.
And He invited them to the garden of life without end;
they died for the sake of Him who came to give life to the human race.
And they trod the way by which humans would go through sufferings to life;
they gave their life for the sake of the Life who gives life to all,
that He might reward them with new life in the kingdom on high.
He sated his wrath, which thirsted for blood, by their slaying,
and thought he had quenched the report of the King by the slaughter;
but the desire of his guile did not come to fulfillment.
For a hidden sign cut them away from the nets of the hunter;
the Babe escaped, on whose account the sword had gone out.
And He came into the open as the proof of prophecy;
Mary, in whose womb the Babe was formed, paid what was due.
She offered a sacrifice, as the law requires for one who opens the womb,
and marked Him with the seal of the house of Abraham upon His members,
that in Him the great covenant of the hope of the peoples might be confirmed.
Behold the demonstration in which the meaning of the words is revealed!
Let us inquire whose flesh it was that a human hand circumcised.
Come, you disputers who have confused the order of flesh and Spirit,
and let us see whose flesh was sealed and offered sacrifices.
If it is the Word who changed Himself and became flesh,
what was it that compelled Him to seal Himself with the seal of men,
so that He received circumcision in His body when He came to be?
In whom were His words to the righteous fulfilled,
that the peoples should become brothers of the house [?]—
and if it is Abraham [?]—
for was it not the body of the house of Abraham that received the seal?

then false also is the promise made to Abram.
If Mary bore not a son of David but the Word,
then explain to us: whose was the body that received the seal?
Or else come, learn, and turn from the perversity of your thoughts.
Why do you wander on a path full of falsehood?
Come along with us, and we will show you the way of peace.
Why do you set yourselves against the goal, facing the Evil One?
Stretch your minds, and consider with us two that became one:
the Word and the body. The Bridegroom's beloved has fixed this goal for us.
Come, let us learn with [?] of soul a single confession.
He wrote that the Word became flesh, not in nature,
but that the Word dwelt in the flesh, the hidden in the manifest.
He said "dwelt," not that he was changed from what he is.
For one cannot both become and dwell, himself, in his own nature;
one can dwell in another in perfect love,
but one alone, how could he dwell in his own hypostasis?
The Word of the Father humbled himself by his will,
and his power dwelt in the pure body that Mary bore;
it was not in his being that he humbled himself and came to birth.
The will of his love was with us in the [?], and called him by his name.
Mary did not give birth to the Being that is hidden from all;
she bore a man who wholly resembles the children of his kind.
Hands did not circumcise the spiritual one who is uncompounded;
it was the bodily one whom bodily hands circumcised.
Mary is a human being, of the humanity of Adam's stock,
and the child born of her resembles her in body and soul.
Mary is equal to other women in her constitution,
but her childbearing is greater than all the births of the daughters of Eve.
Her offspring resembles bodily beings in body and soul,
yet he is holy and more glorious than bodily beings in his constitution.
His nature resembles that of his mother, from whom he is,
and he is higher than she, since his composition was not from seed.
He is wholly man through the completeness of body and soul;
he is also God, since he became the dwelling of the God of all.
He is the son of a human daughter, from whom his composite nature comes;
and he is Son of the Being, made worthy of this by the power of the one who assumed him.
In body and soul he resembles his bodily brothers,
and in authority he is equal with the Word, the Offspring of the Father.
In birth, in conception and in the sufferings of the body he is wholly man;
and in the glories that he received and inherited he is God of all.
My thoughts have not conceived a division into Son and Son.
Let not the heretic find fault with the distinctions in my words:
I have spoken of two natures, distinct one from the other;
I do not count two persons, as the wicked do.
I know the Word of the Father and the body from us as one.
While I worship the spiritual one in the bodily one,
my mind offers one confession, without division.
I kiss the King's robe for the sake of the King;
I have distinguished the natures because of the sufferings and the glories.
One is passible and one impassible: the Word and the body.
Over Mary, and whom she bore, there were disputes;
and for this reason I have drawn back the veil by the distinctions in my words:
the Being has no mother of common flesh.
Why do you trouble the clearness of the truth with the [?] of your wickedness?
The one hidden from all did not come into a [?] existence,

the Unbounded who holds all things, within a limit.
Mary is mother of the second Adam, not of the Being.
Like the earth, she too gave birth without marriage:
the command that signalled to the earth, so that it brought forth Adam,
the same fashioned an image within her members in the likeness of Adam.
He willed to annul the sentence of judgment that had condemned Adam,
and out of the guilty he made a victor and vindicated Adam.
Through the lust of [?] the first one sinned and brought condemnation on his children;
and by self-restraint Adam won the victory in Adam.
Through Mary he annulled that voice in the ears of Eve.
There was death, and here is life that revives Adam.
In Eve's ears the rebel sowed the bitterness of death,
and in Mary's ears the Watcher proclaimed the voice of [?].
He confined Eve in the prison of the pangs of childbirth,
and by the blessings spoken to Mary he lifted the threat.
Because of Adam he cursed the earth, to [?] thorns,
and in the son of Adam he tilled it in glory, so that it would yield glory.
The image that had been defiled by the filth of iniquity he willed to renew;
he recast it in the Spirit and [?] it spiritual gold.
In soul and body mortals sinned and became debtors to sin,
and he set them free through humanity, in body and soul.
For this reason he took a man from a daughter of man,
and armed him with the Spirit to redeem his race from the Strong One.
Henceforth it is right to call the pure one by a name:
mother of the Image in which the hidden nature is [...] made known.
Let us call the child Christ and Son, King and Lord,
the form of a servant that became Lord through the one who assumed him.
And if heretics stumble on the path of my words,
let them contend with him whom I have called Word and body;
from him I learned to call him by the name of servant and Son,
when he said, "Behold, I am going to my Father and my God."
If he is God, how does he go to his God?
And if he is the Maker, how did he receive a second existence?
The Godhead has no God, O heretic!
The Fashioner of all has no maker: hold back your blasphemies!
Be still, do not cry out, [?], head of your ranks.
